# Subtitle font

`V7Subtitles.ttf` is the font libass draws text subtitles with on the PS4 (copied to `/data/PS4IPTV/mpv/subfont.ttf`,
mpv's default subtitle font). It is generated by `scripts/make-subtitle-font.py` (byte-for-byte reproducible;
`--check` verifies the tracked file) from two bundled fonts:

| Part | From | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| every glyph, metric, kerning / layout table and hinting program of Inter SemiBold (Latin incl. Turkish, Greek, Cyrillic) - unchanged | `third_party/inter/Inter-SemiBold.ttf` | SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`LICENSE-OFL.txt`) |
| Arabic (U+0600-06FF), Arabic Presentation Forms A / B, Hebrew (U+0590-05FF) and Hebrew presentation forms, bidi format characters (U+200C-200F, U+202A-202E): 527 code points, outlines without hinting | `third_party/fonts-fallback/DejaVuSans.ttf` | DejaVu's own additions, public domain (`LICENSE-DejaVu.txt`, first line) |
| empty zero-width glyphs for U+061C and U+2066-2069 (bidi format characters neither font has) | generated | - |

The merged font is distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 and named "V7 Subtitles" (it is neither Inter
nor DejaVu). The generator refuses to copy any glyph that DejaVu encodes outside those blocks (the Bitstream Vera /
Arev Latin, Greek and Cyrillic glyphs never come along).

Why one font: the PS4's libass 0.14.0 has no font provider (no fontconfig), so a glyph the subtitle font lacks can
only fall back to that same default font file - and libass 0.14.0 leaves that fallback face's id uninitialised. With
Inter alone, every Arabic letter of every frame repeated the font search and wrote log lines (GitHub issue #1,
"arabic subtitles lag"), and Arabic was drawn as boxes. One font that has every glyph needs no fallback.

Not covered (no bundled font has them in a usable form): CJK, Thai, Indic scripts, emoji, the Urdu letters
U+06C1 / U+06D2. Such characters still show a box; the player no longer writes a log line per glyph per frame.
